summary.summary: Somerset's year-end treasury report shows borrowing of £716m against a £990m ceiling, with everything compliant — but 39.4% of the debt falls due within twelve months, close to the council's own 50% limit, so a large slice must be refinanced at whatever rates arrive. Housing-account financing costs took 11% of housing income this year and the council's own projections take that to 18.3% by 2030/31. The legacy commercial property portfolio (bought for £301m, written down heavily) is being sold off: £33.3m of sales this year at a £4.7m net gain, £82.3m still to go.

compliance.notes: Strong core treasury strategy: an exemplary Arlingclose-style liability benchmark (charted to 2075 and actively used), thorough counterparty/creditworthiness framework, full indicator suite over six years, and a completed exit review of legacy commercial investments. The weak flank is the commercial/non-treasury disclosure set within the supplied papers - no commercial-income-to-revenue ratio (PI-08), no proportionality demonstration (COM-03) and no service/commercial investment limits (COM-09); much of this should live in the separate Non-Treasury Investment Strategy (Appendix T/E), which was not among the supplied PDFs, and the sterling-only borrowing statement (BOR-03) and specified/non-specified categories (INV-05) are also missing from the TMS itself.

news_drafts.headline: Somerset Council's audit fees fall 15% as auditor confirms no new financial complexities
news_drafts.lead: Somerset Council's external audit fees for 2025-26 are £886,658, down from £1,043,816 the previous year after the removal of additional charges. Grant Thornton, the council's auditor, confirmed that there are "no significant new financial reporting matters requiring additional audit time or specialist input", indicating the council has not accumulated new financial complexity during the year. The auditor did identify areas where IT general controls supporting the council's financial systems need strengthening, particularly around access to powerful system functions and separation of responsibilities. The council has accepted the findings and is implementing remediation, including removal of redundant access and strengthened monitoring. Several findings relate to legacy systems that have since been replaced or consolidated, with the council addressing control issues in the replacement systems rather than further investing in systems approaching retirement.
news_drafts.paper_title: Somerset Council IT Audit Report 2026 - Appendices A to I

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee Workplan Sep 26 to May 27
findings.headline: Audit recommendations from the 2024-25 annual report include items that remain overdue and non-compliant.
findings.detail: The Audit Committee has scheduled a specific agenda item for 29 October 2026 titled 'Overdue Actions and Non-Compliance of the AAR'. This confirms the council has audit recommendations from its 2024-25 annual report that have not been implemented on schedule or are not being complied with. Separately, progress against recommendations is tracked at five separate committee meetings across the forward plan (September, November, January, March, May), suggesting ongoing issues with recommendation implementation.
findings.matters: A council scheduling dedicated time to address overdue and non-compliant audit actions signals internal control or governance issues are not being resolved as expected, which affects oversight quality and financial management capability.
findings.quote: Overdue Actions and Non-Compliance of the AAR

findings.paper_title: Somerset Council Pension Fund LGPS Audit Findings Report - 2025-26
findings.headline: Significant volume of disclosure amendments required across 15+ financial statement notes
findings.detail: The auditors identified required amendments in Notes 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 22, 26, 27, 30, and 32. Errors included: incorrect reporting dates used (e.g., 2024 instead of 2026), actuarial assumptions not disclosed, outdated investment manager references, and narrative inconsistencies. All corrections were accepted by management and incorporated.
findings.matters: High volume of disclosure corrections indicates quality control gaps in accounts preparation; while individually non-material, collectively suggests risk of material disclosure misstatement
findings.figures: 15+ notes requiring amendments; all corrections were non-material
findings.quote: The narrative at the bottom of Note 14 referred to assets managed by Brunel of £3,289,163,000 as at 31 March 2025. However, this amount related to assets managed by Brunel as at 31 March 2026.

findings.paper_title: Somerset Council Pension Fund LGPS Audit Findings Report - 2025-26
findings.headline: Material amount of deposits misclassified in prior year requiring restatement of comparative figures
findings.detail: Short-term deposits with other local authorities of £69m in 2024/25 and £75m in 2025/26 were incorrectly classified as Fair Value Through Profit or Loss rather than amortised cost under IFRS 9. The £69m prior year balance was material and comparative figures have been restated. While the classification error had no impact on net assets, it indicates prior-year controls were ineffective.
findings.matters: Material classification error undetected in prior year raises questions about control effectiveness; recurrence in current year suggests systematic weakness in investment review procedures
findings.figures: £69m prior year (material, restated); £75m current year; no impact on net assets of £3,589.7m
findings.quote: The prior year balance of short-term deposits (£69m) was material and, therefore, the comparative figures within Note 18 were required to be restated to reflect the correct classification.

findings.paper_title: Somerset Council Pension Fund LGPS Audit Findings Report - 2025-26
findings.headline: Journal authorization weakness persists after being flagged in 2023/24, 2024/25, and 2025/26 audits
findings.detail: Finance staff can post journal entries without formal authorization or approval by a separate user. The auditors identified this control gap in the 2023/24 audit and repeated the recommendation in 2024/25. In 2025/26, management confirmed no progress has been made on implementing authorization controls.
findings.matters: Absence of authorization creates risk of fraudulent, erroneous, or unauthorized journal entries reaching the ledger; three consecutive years of non-resolution indicates either low risk perception or implementation barriers
findings.figures: Control weakness identified in audit cycles 2023/24, 2024/25, 2025/26
findings.quote: No progress has been made on the implementation of additional authorising of Journals for the 2025/26 financial year.

findings.paper_title: Somerset Council Pension Fund LGPS Audit Findings Report - 2025-26
findings.headline: MS Dynamics 365 and ICON systems have red-rated IT control deficiencies unresolved from prior audit years
findings.detail: The auditors assigned red ratings to both MS Dynamics 365 and ICON (investment management) systems for security management and technology acquisition/development/maintenance. A segregation of duties conflict persists with two users retaining system admin access. These deficiencies were first flagged in 2023/24 and 2024/25 but remain unaddressed.
findings.matters: Weak controls over core financial systems increase risk of undetected fraud, unauthorized access, or data integrity failures; management's failure to remedy three-year-old findings suggests control remediation is not prioritized
findings.figures: Red ITGC ratings on MS Dynamics 365 and ICON systems; 2 users with System Admin access
findings.quote: The segregation of duties conflict remains in place, with two users retaining System Admin access for user administration purposes.
